title: When Envy is a Virtue - Nautilus
gist: Teaser for an essay asking whether envy, long cast as a deadly sin in Biblical, Quranic and evil-eye traditions, can be channeled into a constructive drive for self-improvement; the excerpt covers only the traditional negative view.

insights.claim: Religious and folk traditions across the Middle East, South Asia and the Mediterranean frame envy as dangerous — from Cain killing Abel in the Bible and Quran to amulets worn against the 'evil eye'.
insights.so_what: Context for the piece's contrarian question of whether envy can be a constructive motivator.
insights.quote: a tradition of believing that envious glances can bring tragedy leads some to wear amulets to ward off the so-called evil eye
insights.speaker: Kristen French

insights.claim: The essay poses the contrarian possibility that envy, a 'deadly sin', can help cultivate a constructive drive for self-betterment, though the excerpt does not present the argument.
insights.so_what: Social-comparison as motivation underpins consumer and status-driven spending behavior.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
